Exercise 15.9.45 — Volume of a Bumpy Sphere (Spherical Coordinates)

Problem. The surfaces ρ=1+15sin⁡mθ sin⁡nφ\rho = 1 + \frac{1}{5}\sin m\theta\,\sin n\varphiρ=1+51​sinmθsinnφ have been used as models for tumors. The “bumpy sphere” with m=6m = 6m=6 and n=5n = 5n=5 is shown. Use a computer algebra system to find the volume it encloses.

Part 1 — Volume of the bumpy sphere

Step 1.1: Set up the volume integral.

Because the surface is star-shaped with respect to the origin, the volume enclosed by ρ=1+15sin⁡6θ sin⁡5φ\rho = 1 + \tfrac{1}{5}\sin 6\theta\,\sin 5\varphiρ=1+51​sin6θsin5φ is

V=∫02π∫0π∫01+15sin⁡6θ sin⁡5φρ2sin⁡φ dρ dφ dθ. V = \int_0^{2\pi} \int_0^{\pi} \int_0^{1 + \frac{1}{5}\sin 6\theta\,\sin 5\varphi} \rho^2 \sin\varphi\, d\rho\, d\varphi\, d\theta. V=∫02π​∫0π​∫01+51​sin6θsin5φ​ρ2sinφdρdφdθ.

Step 1.3: Add the surviving terms.

V=4π3+4π99=132π+4π99=136π99. V = \frac{4\pi}{3} + \frac{4\pi}{99} = \frac{132\pi + 4\pi}{99} = \frac{136\pi}{99}. V=34π​+994π​=99132π+4π​=99136π​.

The bumpy sphere encloses slightly more volume than the unit sphere 4π3≈4.18879\tfrac{4\pi}{3} \approx 4.1887934π​≈4.18879, as expected since the sin⁡2\sin^2sin2-term (which adds volume on average) is the only surviving correction.

Step 1.5: Verification by Python.

The script solution/part1_step1.py performs the term-by-term integration with SymPy and then checks the total three independent ways: a high-precision (30-digit) mpmath double quadrature of the unexpanded integrand, which returns 4.315723241295069499302217172994.315723241295069499302217172994.31572324129506949930221717299, matching 136π/99136\pi/99136π/99 to all 25 printed digits; and a fine 2400×16002400 \times 16002400×1600 uniform-grid sum, which agrees to 7×10−77\times 10^{-7}7×10−7. (A single naive SymPy call over the whole double integral is unreliable for this integrand, which is why the term-by-term route is used.)
